textos.titulo: Ten years in the same company
textos.texto: Renata has worked at the same logistics company for ten years. She started as an intern in 2016, when she was still at university. Since then, she has had four different positions and she has been managing a team of twelve people for the last two years. 'People ask me why I've never changed companies,' she says. 'The truth is, I've changed jobs many times — just inside the same company.' Last month, she received an offer from a competitor. She hasn't answered yet.

textos.texto: When I was a kid, my family used to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm. There was no internet and the TV only had two channels, so we used to play outside from morning to night. My grandmother would wake us up early to collect eggs, and my grandfather would tell us stories after dinner. At first, my city friends found it strange. They weren't used to life without shopping malls. Now, as an adult, I'm used to being connected all the time, and I sometimes miss those quiet summers.
perguntas: Where did the family use to spend the summer?

How does the writer feel now?
pessoais: Where did you use to spend your holidays as a child?

textos.texto: When Lucas got off the train, he realized something was wrong. The station didn't look like the photos he had seen online. He checked his ticket and saw that he had taken the train in the opposite direction. By the time he understood the mistake, the last train back had already left. He had never been to that town before and his phone was almost dead. Fortunately, a woman at a café noticed he was lost. She had lived in his city for years, and she offered to drive him to a hotel. Lucas still sends her a message every Christmas.

textos.texto: For decades, people have said that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. But is it true? Some scientists believe that skipping breakfast might help people lose weight, while others argue that it can make us more tired and less productive. The truth is that it probably depends on the person. If you're hungry in the morning, you should eat. If you're not, forcing yourself to eat might not be necessary. What most experts agree on is that what you eat matters more than when you eat it.

What do some scientists believe?
What do others argue?

What do most experts agree on?
pessoais: Do you have breakfast every day? Why?

textos.texto: Last year, a software company in Belo Horizonte decided to test a four-day working week for six months. Before the test, the CEO told employees that salaries would stay the same, but that productivity had to stay the same too. Many managers were worried. One of them said he didn't believe the team could finish everything in four days. Six months later, the results surprised everyone: productivity had increased by 8%, and sick days had fallen by almost half. When journalists asked the CEO if the change would be permanent, she said that unless something unexpected happened, they would never go back.
perguntas: What did the company decide to test?
What did the CEO promise before the test?
What were the managers worried about?
What were the results after six months?
What did the CEO say about making it permanent?
pessoais: Would a four-day week work at your job? Why or why not?

textos.titulo: Learning a language as an adult
textos.texto: Many adults believe it's too late to learn a new language. However, research suggests that adults who study consistently can make faster progress than children in the first months, because they're better at understanding rules and using strategies. What adults usually lack is time and the willingness to make mistakes. Children don't mind sounding silly; adults often avoid speaking until they feel 'ready'. Teachers who work with adults recommend practicing a little every day, focusing on topics that are personally relevant, and accepting mistakes as part of the process.

What do adults usually lack?

What do teachers recommend? Give three things.
pessoais: What has been the hardest part of learning English for you?

textos.texto: Two years ago, Marta left her office job in São Paulo and moved to Lisbon, where she now works remotely for the same company. Although she loves the city, she admits that it hasn't been as easy as she expected. She misses the informal conversations in the office, which used to be where many ideas came from. The time difference is another challenge: her meetings often start at nine in the evening. Despite this, she says she's happier than ever. 'If I had to go back to an office five days a week, I think I'd quit,' she says.

textos.titulo: The ghost of the old theater
textos.texto: The old Municipal Theater was built in 1910 and closed in the 1980s after a fire. For years, it was said to be haunted. Security guards reported hearing music at night, and a woman in a white dress was believed to walk across the stage. In 2019, the building was finally restored. During the renovation, workers found a box of old letters that had been hidden under the stage. They had been written by a young actress who had died in the fire. Since the letters were published, the strange noises have stopped — or so people say.

textos.texto: When Felipe turned twenty-five, his uncle advised him to start investing a small part of his salary every month. Felipe laughed. He was earning well, he was young, and he wanted to enjoy life. Fifteen years later, he did the math. If he had followed his uncle's advice, he would have had enough savings to buy an apartment without a loan. 'I wish I hadn't been so arrogant,' he says today. 'And I wish schools taught financial education.' He now gives his own nephews the same advice — and he's not sure they're listening either.

Why didn't Felipe follow the advice?

textos.texto: Last month, a law firm submitted a document to a court that contained references to cases that didn't exist. The lawyer had used an AI tool to write it and hadn't checked the sources. The judge fined the firm and said the lawyer should have verified every reference. Supporters of AI argue that the tool wasn't the problem — the person was. Critics, on the other hand, say that companies must have known that their tools sometimes invent information, and that they should have warned users more clearly. Either way, the case raises an important question: who is responsible when AI makes a mistake?

Why did it happen?
What did the judge say?
What do supporters of AI argue?
What do critics say about the companies?
pessoais: Who do you think is responsible when AI makes a mistake?

textos.texto: Urban planners in Curitiba believe that by 2040, the city will have changed more than in the previous fifty years. Most private cars will have been replaced by electric buses and shared vehicles, and several central streets will have been closed to traffic. Residents will be living closer to their workplaces, as offices are expected to be spread across neighborhoods rather than concentrated downtown. However, not everyone is optimistic. Some economists warn that, unless housing prices are controlled, these changes will benefit mainly the wealthy, while poorer families will have been pushed further from the center.

pessoais: How will your city have changed by 2040?

textos.texto: We tend to assume that more options make us happier. Yet psychologist Barry Schwartz argues the opposite. In a famous experiment, a supermarket offered customers samples of either six or twenty-four types of jam. Although the larger display attracted more attention, people who saw only six options were about ten times more likely to buy. Schwartz calls this the 'paradox of choice': when faced with too many alternatives, we become anxious, delay decisions and feel less satisfied with what we finally choose, since we keep imagining that another option might have been better. Critics point out that later studies haven't always reproduced the effect; nevertheless, the idea has influenced everything from restaurant menus to streaming platforms.
